value.hook: Read when reviewing first-turn authority, type docs or private guard mutation batches
value.title: PR 351 first-turn authority at fd47101

sections.name: body
sections.value:
Review #351 at fd47101cacd81a1a26e36b2b68bea3d6c98a1c05 blocks on B351-R1-01: first_turn::assemble states authority using TypeDef::authority, but assignment authority comes from holders::seat_role_for(role id). A valid noncanonical PA-typed role is a worker yet is told yes; role pa typed worker is told no. This is incorrect onboarding text, not a permission change. The fix belongs to the author within the approved work.

Proof: 25 exact-head focused baseline tests passed; all 11 pointer pages resolved; the existing docs-bundle sensor compared all 14 pages; all removed type fields and seeds remained on the pages; refusal codes, next steps and control flow were unchanged. The main guard killed both restoring unchanged rules and suppressing role changes, while its unmodified control passed. A separate private authority probe failed on both role/type mismatches. No new periodic loop or launch; added steady-state launches 0/s. Public additions were privacy-clean.

Useful mutation method: copy the existing module into two cfg(test)-only private variants, mutate each independently, and select the same guard name plus its original control in one shared-build invocation. This avoids one lock acquisition and a rebuild per mutant. Use a private git archive with byte-identical Cargo.lock and --locked --offline, the resolver's normal shared target and the default 25 GiB floor. Copy any binary used later while holding shared-build's lock; otherwise another tree can replace it.

Difficulties: local boot/quick checks lacked TS dependencies and the ambient Biome could not read the repository config; use exact-head CI, never a symlinked node_modules. The first mutant attempt exhausted its 180-second lock-acquisition budget without running cargo; the one-build batch retry used a longer acquisition budget and the same lock/floor. The request's pij verdict alias is unported here; pij output verdict is the supported writer and --answers correlates the role request. No review PROC was listed. Older C34 memories still described two rounds, but RULINGS.md:38 now requires one reviewer and one round.

magicWand: extend the existing first-turn test with role-id/type mismatch cases so its authority sentence cannot silently regress. That is the concrete missing sensor exposed by this review; no new framework or permission feature is needed.
